name: Thermal state and headroom
plain: Reports how hot the device is: 4 coarse levels on iOS, 7 levels plus a forecast on Android.
meaning: Shows the phone is throttled or in a hot place (car, sun, charging while gaming). Weak context signal; more useful to games that scale quality.

android.note: Status: NONE, LIGHT, MODERATE, SEVERE, CRITICAL, EMERGENCY, SHUTDOWN (7 levels); headroom is a 0.0 to 1.0 float forecast, 1.0 meaning throttling

limits.headline: Can tell how hot your phone is, in 4 levels on iPhone and 7 on Android
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app checks while it is running, mostly games and video
can: See iPhone heat as nominal, fair, serious or critical
See Android heat in 7 levels, from none to shutdown
Get a forecast on Android 11 and newer, as a number from 0.0 to 1.0
Slow down graphics or work when the phone is hot
cannot: See an exact temperature in degrees on iPhone
See heat forecasts on Android 10 and older
limits.differs: Android gives 7 levels plus a forecast. iPhone gives 4 coarse levels only.

story.what_it_is: An app can tell if your phone is getting too hot.

marketing.name: Thermal API and ADPF
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: sense heat headroom so games and apps can adjust before the phone slows down.

marketing.name: Thermal state
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: apps can respond to the device's thermal state to keep it cool and responsive.

story.for_you: If your phone gets hot in a car or in the sun, a game may lower its graphics so it cools down. You see a smoother, cooler experience, though sometimes with fewer effects.
story.for_makers: Games and video apps use it to scale quality before the phone throttles and stutters. Android offers seven levels and a forecast, iOS four coarse levels.

use_cases.example: A racing game quietly cuts shadows and resolution when your phone reports heat, so frame rate holds.
An AR app drops tracking quality when your phone is hot after a long session.
A camera or video call app lowers resolution if the phone is overheating.
A workout app that uses camera and GPS warns you the phone is too hot in the sun.
A car mirror app on a hot dashboard reduces map detail to stay cool.
A streaming app lowers bitrate when the phone is hot during a long live stream.

story.android_note: Reports seven levels plus a forecast of future headroom.
story.ios_note: Reports four coarse levels to apps.

technical_bounds: No temperature in degrees on iOS
Headroom rate-limited: call at most about once per second
